title: De Vita Libri Tres (Latin, 1549)
author: Marsilio Ficino
description: De Vita Libri Tres (Three Books on Life) by Marsilio Ficino (1433-1499), the Florentine priest, physician and translator of Plato, Plotinus and the Corpus Hermeticum, here in a Latin edition of 1549, 'freed from errors' and with additions. First published in 1489, it is a medical and magical guide addressed to scholars, whose melancholic temperament (associated with Saturn) endangers their health. Book I, On a Healthy Life, gives advice on diet, sleep, exercise and remedies for learned people. Book II, On a Long Life, covers prolonging life in old age. Book III, On Obtaining Life from the Heavens, a commentary on Plotinus, explains how to draw down beneficial celestial influences through the world spirit by means of music, images, talismans, plants, stones, scents and colours. It is the central text of Renaissance natural and astrological magic and influenced Agrippa, Bruno and Campanella.
